# Goban Studio v4.0.0

v4 is about refinement: a calm board, an interface built from one written
design system, the standard 19×19 board everywhere, and reviews that walk
you through what happened.

## Download and first launch

<!-- first-launch -->
| Platform | File | First launch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `GobanStudio-macOS-arm64.dmg` or `.zip` | See the package README. |
| Windows (x64) | `GobanStudio-Windows-x64.zip` | See the package README. |
<!-- /first-launch -->

`SHA256SUMS` lists the checksums of all three files.

## The board

- **No more texture by default.** The board is a calm, plain honey colour
  with a barely-there falloff. *Light wood* keeps the grain at a quarter of
  its old strength; *Ink* is a dark board for dark rooms. The other surfaces
  are gone.
- **Crisp lines.** Grid lines are snapped to whole screen pixels, the frame
  is a little heavier, star points and stones follow a written specification,
  and stones sit on the board with a short, soft shadow.
- **The standard board everywhere.** A first game, the onboarding game, the
  suggested game and the New game sheet all start on 19×19, with a handicap
  from your level; 13×13 and 9×9 are offered as quicker games. The sheet
  remembers the size you chose. Coordinates are on by default.

## The interface

- **One design system** (`docs/design.md`): system fonts in every language,
  an 8 px grid, neutral colours with a single accent, and one primary action
  per screen.
- **A desktop shell**: a labelled sidebar, and a toolbar with back/forward,
  breadcrumbs and the place's actions. On macOS the window has a tall,
  hidden title bar and the toolbar sits beside the traffic lights.
- **Recomposed screens**: Today starts from one hero (continue, or the
  suggested game) and a short list; Practice shows the next lesson, today's
  five and the course without noise; the Play panel has fixed places for
  players, status, actions and the move list; Review puts the balance chart
  first and moves its tools to the toolbar.
- **Dark mode** and the Ink board were checked side by side; every colour
  token is tested for contrast in light and dark.

## Reviewing

- **What went wrong, and where**: each key mistake says whether a group
  died, a capturing race or ko was lost, territory was given away or a big
  point was missed, and how many points each area cost.
- **Step by step**: open a mistake to play the better line, or what happens
  as played, one described move at a time ("White ataris the two stones",
  "Black captures 3 stones"…). ←/→ step through it; captured stones leave
  the board.

## Practice

- **Seki and capturing races.** The solver now recognises seki: new problems
  ask you to live in seki, and a kill that only reaches seki is shown as
  such. Capturing races cover outside and shared liberties, eye against no
  eye, and big eye against small eye.
- **Classic shapes**: straight and bent three, pyramid four, bulky and
  crossed five, rabbity and rectangular six, the second-line group — as a
  collection of their own.
- **Proved on a real board.** Every problem was re-proved with captured
  points playable again (as on a real board) and with no life borrowed from
  outside the problem. 17 problems were corrected and 37 removed because
  they did not hold under those rules; 262 problems remain, each still
  proved by the solver (`docs/problems-audit.md`).
- A beginner's daily five only uses topics their finished lessons taught;
  a wrong answer resets itself and says so.

## Playing

- **Count** is in the game's ⋯ menu, so any game can be brought to the
  count.
- Sound levels are balanced (captures quieter than the stone, the result in
  between); the computer's pace suits a 19×19 game.

## Updates

- **Help → Check for updates…** asks GitHub for the latest release, once,
  when you choose it. A weekly automatic check can be turned on in Settings;
  it is off by default. Nothing about you or your games is sent.

## Quality

- Real-browser checks now also enforce one primary button per screen, and
  visual baselines use a pinned test font so they compare layout, not the
  runner's fonts.
- The packaged apps are launched in CI and screenshotted on macOS and
  Windows (Today, a 19×19 game, its review, Practice, Settings).
- A string sheet for native-speaker review (`docs/l10n/`).

## Known limits

- The packaged apps are signed only if the project's certificates are set
  up (`docs/signing.md`); the table above says what this build actually is.
- The sidebar is not translucent (vibrancy): the system WebView cannot blur
  the window behind it, and Native SDK 0.11 exposes no vibrancy API.
- Sound levels and the computer's pace were tuned from the design rules,
  not yet on a range of real machines.
- The usability test with real people has still not been run
  (`docs/usability.md` says what was done instead).
- No native speaker has reviewed the Chinese, Korean or Japanese text yet
  (`docs/l10n/README.md`).

## Your data

Everything from v3 carries over. The old kaya, paper and katsura boards
become Plain or Light wood, slate becomes Ink, and coordinates are turned on
unless you had changed the board yourself.
